discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany (EPTA)

motivation: Over two decades, pulsar timing arrays turned millisecond pulsars into a galaxy-sized gravitational-wave detector. In 2023 NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA and PPTA independently reported a common red-noise process with the Hellings-Downs angular correlation, the smoking-gun signature of a stochastic gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies. This opens a new window on the Universe, complementary to LIGO and the future LISA. The signal is most naturally attributed to supermassive black-hole binaries, yet it already constrains early-universe sources such as first-order phase transitions and cosmic strings, making cosmology testable in a new band. The achievement rests on patient, long-term effort: decades of precision timing, instrument development, noise modelling and community-built analysis tools. McLaughlin, Kramer and Manchester led and sustained the three founding collaborations whose combined work established this result.
